accuracy.evidence: Checked against DfE statutory Relationships, Sex and Health Education guidance (primary Health Education, Mental wellbeing: recognise and talk about emotions, simple self-care techniques, where and how to seek support), the PSHE Association Key Stage 1 programme on change and loss and the feelings they bring, and the IB PYP PSPE identity strand cited by the topic. Advice to keep routines steady, name changes honestly and talk to a trusted adult follows NHS and Young Minds guidance on supporting children through change.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented slips for young children facing transitions: believing only one feeling is allowed (mixed-feelings prediction, Mia's heart and the onefeel tag), keeping a worry secret (helper prediction and secret tag), coping by hiding or lashing out (tools step and hide and shout tags), confusing daily routines with changes (spot step), and assuming everything changes when much stays the same (sort step and the new tag).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagadapt models a life transition itself: a change-or-routine tap grid, a heart that holds several feelings at once and names them together, a changes versus stays-the-same sort for a school move, a ring of people around Leo where only trusted adults connect, and a worry meter that only falls with healthy coping tools. The shingle gate passed against every lab, including flagcope, flagcalm and flagchange.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds that brushing teeth is refused as a change, sees two and then three feelings sit together in Mia's heart with the words Sad + Excited, discovers that home things stay the same at a new school, sees the stranger and the TV turned down while trusted adults connect to Leo, and watches the worry meter drop only for helpful tools.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with a tempting wrong option: only one feeling at a time, keeping a worry secret, and hiding under the bed. The heart then holds two feelings at once, the trusted-adult links appear only for people Leo can tell, and the worry meter falls with a teddy and talking but not with hiding, before the done message echoes the prediction.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with nine tagged wrong-answer messages (same, same2, onefeel, hide, secret, stranger, shout, new). Each names the slip, for example you can have two feelings at once, or keeping it secret makes it feel bigger so tell a grown-up you trust.

readability.evidence: Family audience: kid paragraphs score about FK 0.4 against the 5.0 target with very short sentences and concrete words such as new baby, teddy and slow breaths; adult paragraphs score about FK 6.9 against 10.0 and still use the terms routine, mixed feelings, trusted adult and coping tool.

no_filler.evidence: Content gate passed with no filler phrases and explanation overlap under 12 percent, including against Choosing the Right Coping Strategy, Simple Calming Strategies and Feelings Change and Differ. Each adult paragraph carries curriculum references, defined words, named mistakes or what the lab does, and items explain why each wrong option does not help.

mobile.evidence: Walkthrough passed on iPhone 13 and desktop. Screenshots at 390 px in light and dark themes show large emoji tap cards in two columns, the heart and four feeling faces fitting the width, the five-person ring around Leo without overlap, and the worry meter above six tool cards; every action has a big button below the canvas.

accessibility.evidence: axe-core reports no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in either theme. The canvas aria-label is rewritten with every message, every tap or drag has a labelled button (for example Is it a change? Get a new teacher, or Talk to Grandma), canvas text uses the theme text colour on white or pale tiles in light mode and slate tiles in dark mode, and reduced motion shortens the auto-play.

International Baccalaureate (2018) PYP personal, social and physical education scope and sequence: Identity
NHS (2023) Every Mind Matters and Young Minds guidance: helping children cope with change, starting school and moving house
